narrative.overview: The browser becomes a calibrated viewing instrument: a quiet paper-colored room surrounding one optically dominant black image field. Controls remain physically attached to the image, and the interface earns trust through restraint rather than ornamental chrome.
keyCharacteristics: One integrated control chassis and imaging field.
Paper, graphite, cobalt, and imaging black as the complete visual world.
One-pixel structural rules instead of nested cards.
Dense controls with generous reading space around the instrument.
Motion clarifies arrival, state, and disclosure, then gets out of the way.

rules.name: The Cobalt Restraint Rule
rules.body: Cobalt appears only for primary action, selection, focus, and live tool state; the image remains chromatically neutral.

rules.name: The One Instrument Voice Rule
rules.body: Outfit is the only typeface; hierarchy comes from scale, weight, line height, and negative tracking.

rules.name: The Flat Instrument Rule
rules.body: Internal modules never receive independent card shadows; depth belongs to the complete instrument or transient feedback.

dos: Do keep controls physically attached to the image field so the interface reads as one instrument.
Do reserve cobalt for primary action, selection, focus, and active operational state.
Do use one-pixel rules and contrast before adding depth.
Do preserve 44px minimum interactive targets and the reduced-motion path.
Do let the black viewport remain the dominant visual mass whenever an image can be inspected.
donts: Don't turn tool groups, metadata, or privacy disclosures into separate floating cards.
Don't add gradients, decorative glass, or independent shadows to internal modules.
Don't introduce a second decorative accent or use Clear-Session Red outside destructive state.
Don't replace Outfit with an editorial display pairing or all-caps dashboard typography.
Don't soften the instrument into oversized pills; reserve the full pill for the optical aperture.
